meeting.title: ChowNow weekly sync — parity crunch
meeting.summary: Weekly sync with ChowNow ahead of go-live in ~10 days. Down to the last 3 dashboards showing small variances against Tableau. Traced two of them to a timezone cast — order timestamps are stored UTC but the Tableau extracts were localised to Pacific, so day-boundary counts drift. Kevin will confirm the third is the same root cause. Once the fix is validated we can run the go-live readiness review. SSO and guardrails are already done; parity is the only open gate.
action_items: Kevin to confirm the third dashboard variance is the same timezone-cast root cause by Wednesday
Caroline to push the timezone fix to staging and re-run the parity checks
Lucia to give final parity sign-off once all three dashboards match
Sandra to keep the go-live comms draft ready to send the moment parity signs off
key_decisions: Order-timestamp metrics standardise on UTC in the semantic layer; the dashboard localises for display
Go-live readiness review is gated only on parity sign-off — everything else is green
meeting.notes: Genuine crunch but well-managed. Kevin is sharp — he'd already half-diagnosed the timezone issue before the call. Lucia is ready to sign the moment numbers match. The readiness review can't start until parity clears, so this is the single blocker.

transcript.speaker: You
transcript.text: Ten days out. The only thing standing between us and the readiness review is parity, so let's spend the whole call there. Kevin, where are we?

transcript.speaker: Kevin O'Rourke
transcript.text: Three dashboards still off, all by tiny amounts on day-boundary counts. I think it's timezones — our order timestamps are UTC in the warehouse, but the old Tableau extracts were localised to Pacific, so an order at 11pm Pacific lands on the next day in ours.

transcript.speaker: You
transcript.text: That would do it exactly. The right fix is to standardise the metric on UTC in the semantic layer and localise only at display time — not to bend the model to match the old extract.

transcript.speaker: Kevin O'Rourke
transcript.text: Agreed. Two of the three are definitely this. Let me confirm the third is the same and not a separate bug — I'll have that by Wednesday.

transcript.speaker: You
transcript.text: I'll push the timezone fix to staging today and re-run the parity checks. If all three line up, Lucia, are you good to sign off?

transcript.speaker: Lucia Herrera
transcript.text: The second the numbers match I'll sign. I don't want to be the one holding up go-live over a rounding difference, but I also won't sign on a variance I can't explain — and now we can explain it.

transcript.speaker: You
transcript.text: That's the right bar. Sandra, keep the rollout comms drafted so we can send the moment parity clears — I don't want comms to be the new bottleneck.

transcript.speaker: Sandra Kim
transcript.text: Comms are drafted and scheduled as a draft — one click when you give the word.

transcript.speaker: You
transcript.text: Then the plan is: Kevin confirms Wednesday, I validate the fix, Lucia signs, we book the readiness review. Thanks all.
